rfi.title: UN backs effort to drop Mercator map and show size of Africa more accurately
rfi.description: The United Nations voted on Saturday for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting the true size of countries.

rfi.title: A nation trapped: photographing the broken promises of Sudan's revolution
rfi.description: Syrian-born photographer Abdulmonam Eassa travelled to Sudan as the fall of its longtime dictator, toppled by massive protests, raised hopes of a democratic rebirth. Instead, he witnessed the country descend into another military takeover, rivalry and all-out war. RFI spoke to him about the resulting photo series, War in Sudan: A Nation Trapped, which is now on show at the Visa pour l'Image festival in southern France.

rfi.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow to thrash out plan to end war in Ukraine
rfi.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the envoys of the US president Donald Trump, landed in Moscow on Saturday to discuss proposals to end more than four years of war between Russia and Ukraine.

rfi.title: PSG boss Enrique plays down slow start to Ligue 1 campaign after Monaco defeat
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain head coach Luis Enrique on Saturday played down his side's faltering start to the 2026/2027 Ligue 1 season following a 2-1 home defeat to Monaco.

rfi.title: Paris 'Dragon Ball' theme park in doubt as Japanese owners deny granting licence
rfi.description: The Japanese rights holders for the Dragon Ball anime franchise have denied giving permission for a theme park in the Paris region based on the popular series. The confusion follows French President Emmanuel Macron's announcement of a deal with Saudi Arabia to build three parks outside the capital.

rfi.title: Data-rich systems and weak security: why France is a target for cyberattacks
rfi.description: France is one of Europe's biggest targets for cyberattacks. While its political and economic importance make it a mark for foreign governments, criminals are increasingly exploiting gaps in cybersecurity to access the vast amounts of personal data in the country's interconnected public systems.

rfi.title: How China’s Paracel expansion extends its military reach towards Vietnam
rfi.description: China is rapidly expanding two artificial islands in the disputed Paracel Islands, with analysts saying the new facilities could strengthen Beijing’s military reach towards Vietnam and along key South China Sea shipping routes.

rfi.title: DRC eyes Jerusalem embassy as Tshisekedi seeks Israel's support
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo plans to move its embassy in Israel from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem following talks between President Félix Tshisekedi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a rare diplomatic step that could also strengthen Kinshasa's ties with Washington and its access to military support.

rfi.title: France unveils €1.1bn emergency aid for farmers after record heat
rfi.description: ​France has announced €1.1 billion in emergency aid for farmers after record heat and drought caused severe damage to crops, pastures and water supplies.

rfi.title: How France and Britain’s far right are building a populist ‘entente cordiale’
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella will address Reform UK's party conference in Birmingham on Friday, putting the French far-right leader alongside Nigel Farage as both men seek to strengthen their political profiles. The appearance also marks closer ties between two of Europe's most successful populist radical-right parties that share similar positions on immigration but have not always been natural allies.

rfi.title: Paris families sue mayor over alleged child abuse in after-school care
rfi.description: Around 15 families who allege their children suffered violence and sexual abuse in Paris after-school care have filed a complaint against the city and its Socialist mayor, Emmanuel Grégoire, as well as his predecessor Anne Hidalgo.

rfi.title: Tunisia court upholds long sentences in mass trial of opposition figures
rfi.description: Tunisia's top court has turned down the final appeal of dozens of opposition leaders, lawyers and businessmen convicted in a major conspiracy case, in a ruling opponents said further entrenches President Kais Saied's authoritarian rule.

rfi.title: France tests Tesla's self-driving tech as Europe moves closer to autonomous cars
rfi.description: France is preparing to test Tesla’s self-driving system on public roads, a move that could bolster the technology's chances of winning approval throughout the European Union.

rfi.title: British, French leaders hold talks on migrants and EU relations
rfi.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron held their first official talks on Thursday, with migrant boats, Ukraine and British-EU relations high on the agenda.

rfi.title: Former RFI journalist disappears in Niger after attempted coup
rfi.description: Reporters Without Borders has called for an investigation into the disappearance of Moussa Kaka, the director of a television station in Niger and a former correspondent for Radio France International, days after a failed coup in the country.

rfi.title: France asserts sovereignty over disputed Pacific islands as Vanuatu turns to ICJ
rfi.description: France has insisted on its sovereignty over two Pacific islands claimed by Vanuatu, which has opened a case at the International Court of Justice.

rfi.title: EU lawmakers demand Brussels force Meta to 'protect' European children
rfi.description: European Union lawmakers have demanded that the bloc's executive compel Meta to change the "addictive" design of its platforms in Europe, as the giant has promised to do in some US states, according to a letter seen by the French news agency AFP on Thursday.

rfi.title: Three Pacific hurricanes gather strength as El Nino intensifies
rfi.description: The current El Nino could become the strongest on record as the natural climate pattern that warms the tropical Pacific intensifies, with three hurricanes churning across the ocean on Thursday. The United Nations has warned of growing extreme weather risks into 2027.

euronews.title: Paris drops Mercator projection: France now looks smaller on world maps
euronews.description: France is redrawing its world map: deeming the Mercator projection misleading, the foreign ministry will drop it in favour of a map that better reflects actual continental sizes, especially Africa.

euronews.title: US drafting post-war plan for the Middle East, report says
euronews.description: Axios reported that the plan remains in its early stages but that it could set out US policy towards the Middle East for the remainder of Trump's term.

euronews.title: Spain to maintain border checks on arrivals from Italy until 22 September
euronews.description: Spain's Interior Ministry has extended checks on travellers arriving from Italy for a further 15 days, until 22 September, mirroring Rome's move after the Ceuta migration crisis.

euronews.title: Beer production in the EU: rankings, trends and curiosities
euronews.description: The latest Eurostat figures show a trend: beer production is slowly declining year after year. Germany leads in 2025, closely followed by Spain.

euronews.description: On Friday, the financial agency raised Portugal's debt rating from "A" to "A+", with a "stable" outlook, the agency said in a published note.

euronews.title: Two people pulled alive by Nepal's search and rescue team 10 days after devastating flash floods
euronews.description: Ten days after floods devastated Nepal, one woman and one man were pulled alive on Saturday in separate search and rescue operations. Meanwhile, more than 5,000 people remain missing and at least 1,300 were killed.

euronews.title: Bosnian Serb war criminal Mladić commemorated in Belgrade, but no state honours
euronews.description: Thousands are expected at Mladić's burial in Belgrade on Monday, which will proceed without serving officials, artillery salutes or ceremonial military presence. Brussels has earlier said any glorification would be "incompatible with the values on which the EU path is built".

euronews.title: 'Protest' at Port of Dover causes delays to ferry services as masked men descend on the town

euronews.description: The German economy has been in crisis for years. Writes Nikolas Stihl in an OpEd für Euronews. Better business conditions are the key to breaking out of this stagnation. euronews.title: Medieval manuscripts made from animal skin reveal ancient history of deadly sheep virus
euronews.description: Hidden in the pages of medieval manuscripts, researchers have found DNA traces of a deadly sheep virus dating back thousands of years.

euronews.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had earlier said Ukraine would hold off on strikes while Witkoff and Kushner made the trip, while calling on Moscow to do the same.

lemonde.title: Vladimir Poutine, chef de guerre et chef de campagne électorale, prépare la Russie à une escalade militaire
lemonde.description: Pour la première fois depuis l’invasion de l’Ukraine en février 2022, les Russes élisent leurs députés entre les 18 et 20 septembre. Orchestré par le Kremlin, ce scrutin n’a pas d’enjeu électoral et est avant tout un instrument pour mobiliser à la guerre.

lemonde.title: En Saxe-Anhalt, la forêt menacée, nouveau terrain d’offensive pour l’extrême droite à la veille des élections régionales
lemonde.description: Dans le Harz, en Saxe-Anhalt, la sécheresse et les scolytes ont détruit jusqu’à 90 % des épicéas depuis 2018. Alors que l’AfD est donnée en tête des élections régionales du 6 septembre, le combat pour reboiser cette forêt meurtrie est devenu, malgré lui, un enjeu politique.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : pour Gabriel Attal et Edouard Philippe, le poids d’un bilan écologique contrasté
lemonde.description: « Les candidats et le climat ». Les deux principaux aspirants du bloc central défendent une vision pragmatique de l’adaptation climatique, qui marierait croissance et écologie. A Matignon, ils avaient surtout privilégié l’économie.

lemonde.title: Fiscalité : de plus en plus de communes ciblent les résidences secondaires
lemonde.description: Un nombre croissant de villes et villages de tout bord politique augmentent la taxe sur les résidences secondaires. Au total, elle a rapporté 3 milliards d’euros en 2025. Mais le mouvement suscite une fraude non négligeable.

lemonde.title: Zinédine Zidane maintient sa confiance à l’ex-policier détaché auprès des Bleus, dans le collimateur de la justice
lemonde.description: Visé par une information judiciaire pour avoir reçu un chèque de 60 000 euros de Kylian Mbappé en 2023, sanctionné disciplinairement fin 2025 avec une mise à la retraite anticipée, l’ancien CRS continuera à œuvrer à la sécurité des Bleus au sein du staff du nouveau sélectionneur, aux côtés d’un fonctionnaire de police.

lemonde.title: Foire aux vins 2026 : notre sélection des 100 meilleures bouteilles de la rentrée
lemonde.description: Nos journalistes ont goûté plus de 300 vins proposés par 23 enseignes (supermarchés, caves, sites Internet) et en ont retenu 100, dont 43 % en bio ou en biodynamie. Un tiers des bouteilles sont à moins de 10 euros.

lemonde.title: En Israël, les divisions religieuses entre juifs s’invitent dans la campagne des élections législatives
lemonde.description: La ville de Jérusalem vit de plus en plus sous la pression des juifs ultraorthodoxes et des sionistes qui souhaitent imposer leurs revendications religieuses.

lemonde.title: Au Kenya, le président Ruto exige la fermeture des petits commerces tenus par des étrangers
lemonde.description: Une coalition de plusieurs organisations de défense des droits humains a dénoncé, vendredi 4 septembre, une décision « inconstitutionnelle » qui risque « d’encourager les discriminations et le profilage xénophobe ».

lemonde.title: Pollution marine : « Réduire la production de plastique est bien plus efficace que de chercher à nettoyer les océans »
lemonde.description: Différentes initiatives ont vu le jour pour retirer les déchets plastiques qui souillent les océans. Le financement de certaines d’entre elles est aussi, pour des acteurs du secteur pétrochimique, une façon de faire oublier leur participation à cette pollution, alors qu’ils s’opposent à la création d’un instrument international juridiquement contraignant, souligne, dans une tribune au « Monde », le consultant Pierre-Maël Deffontaines.

lemonde.title: Les Chinois délaissent les oiseaux en cage au profit de l’observation en plein air
lemonde.description: L’observation des oiseaux en liberté connaît un essor fulgurant dans les grandes villes chinoises, supplantant l’ancienne tradition de les maintenir en cage. Dans les campagnes, ce phénomène permet de développer le tourisme ornithologique.

lemonde.title: A Monaco, Thierry Lacoste, ex-avocat du prince Albert II, mis en examen pour corruption
lemonde.description: Cette mise en cause ouvre un nouvel épisode de la bataille judiciaire qui secoue la principauté depuis la publication, en 2021, des « dossiers du Rocher ».

lemonde.title: En Haïti, les autorités impuissantes à endiguer la violence des gangs à l’approche des élections
lemonde.description: Plus de 3 000 personnes ont été tuées durant les six premiers mois de l’année, malgré le déploiement progressif d’une nouvelle force multinationale. Les exactions des groupes criminels font planer le doute sur la tenue, en décembre, des élections présidentielle et législatives, les premières organisées dans le pays depuis dix ans.

lemonde.title: Le Top 14 fait marche arrière et revient à la règle des huit remplacements par match
lemonde.description: Les entraîneurs du championnat de France de rugby vont devoir changer leurs habitudes pour la nouvelle saison, qui commence samedi, eux qui avaient le droit à 12 changements par rencontre depuis 2018.

lemonde.title: Teddy Riner, blessé à l’épaule, déclare forfait pour les Championnats du monde de judo
lemonde.description: Le triple champion olympique en individuel ne fera pas son retour sur les tatamis lors du tournoi organisé à Bakou, du 4 au 11 octobre, a annoncé la Fédération française de judo, samedi. Il voit ainsi s’envoler l’occasion de décrocher un douzième titre mondial.

lemonde.title: Merveille, la chanteuse propulsée depuis la porte de Clignancourt : « Dans le groupe de garçons avec qui je faisais de la musique, certains étaient grave jaloux »
lemonde.description: « La Relève ». Chaque mois, « Le Monde » rencontre un jeune qui bouscule les normes dans son domaine. A seulement 18 ans, l’artiste s’est déjà frayé un chemin dans le paysage musical français.

lemonde.title: Isabel Coixet, réalisatrice de « Trois adieux » : « Je ne veux pas marteler le spectateur avec des émotions »
lemonde.description: A l’occasion de la sortie de son nouveau film, la cinéaste espagnole évoque, dans un entretien au « Monde », la création, le quotidien et les petites obsessions qui dirigent son travail.

france24fr.title: Élections en Israël : un superflic juif candidat sur une liste arabe, une "révolution"
france24fr.description: Yoav Segalovitz, un ancien policier et ministre juif, sera numéro deux sur la liste du parti arabe israélien Ra'am aux élections du 27 octobre 2026. Cette annonce faite le 31 août détonne dans un climat électoral où l'extrême droite stigmatise toujours plus les Palestiniens citoyens d'Israël. Elle pourrait cependant ouvrir la voie à l'inclusion d'un parti arabe dans une coalition d'opposition à Netanyahu et ses alliés.

france24fr.title: Visite des émissaires américains : Poutine ordonne l'arrêt des frappes sur Kiev pendant trois jours
france24fr.description: Le président russe Vladimir Poutine a ordonné, samedi, de cesser les frappes sur Kiev pendant trois jours, alors que les Américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner doivent s'y rendre. Les deux émissaires du président américain ont atterri à Moscou avec un plan visant à mettre fin à plus de quatre ans de guerre en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Plus de 5 000 disparus au Népal : des familles tentent de faire leur deuil
france24fr.description: Au Népal, le dernier bilan de la crue meurtrière après l’effondrement d’une partie d’un glacier est de 1 287 morts et 5 083 disparus selon l’autorité népalaise chargée de la gestion des situations d’urgence. De nombreuses familles tentent de faire le deuil de leurs proches, malgré parfois l’absence de corps. Notre envoyée spéciale au Népal, Ondine de Gaulle, s’est rendue sur le site de crémation Pashupati Aryaghat à Katmandou.

france24fr.title: Au Népal, que sait-on des deux rescapés de la catastrophe samedi ?
france24fr.description: Les secours népalais sont parvenus samedi à extraire une personne, de nationalité chinoise, d'un tunnel du nord du pays où il était retenu prisonnier depuis la coulée de boue meurtrière du 26 août, après qu'un pan d'un glacier ce soit effondré. Par ailleurs, les services du Premier ministre népalais ont annoncé samedi le sauvetage d'une femme de 64 ans, Chandrika Shrestha, retrouvée vivante dans une maison de la localité sinistrée de Betrawati.

france24fr.title: Amnesty international alerte sur la détention en Arabie saoudite du franco-égyptien Amr Abdelfattah
france24fr.description: Ingénieur-chercheur franco-égyptien en télécommunications, Amr Abdelfattah est détenu en Arabie saoudite depuis juin 2024, après avoir été arrêté lors d’un pèlerinage à La Mecque. Présenté à la justice saoudienne en mai 2025, il a finalement été condamné à huit ans de prison, notamment pour avoir prétendument insulté le gouvernement saoudien. Amnesty International plaide pour sa libération. Les précisions avec Julia Basile, avocate d’Amr Abdelfattah, invitée de France 24.

france24fr.title: Moules, frites et politique : ambiance présidentielle à la braderie de Lille
france24fr.description: Trois candidats à la présidentielle participent, samedi, à la braderie de Lille, plaçant l'événement populaire au cœur de la campagne pour les élections de 2027. Gabriel Attal et Marine Tondelier sont venus à la rencontre des électeurs ce matin, tandis que Jean-Luc Mélenchon est attendu vers 16 h pour un discours.

france24fr.title: Handicap en France : Emmanuel Macron annonce une série de mesures
france24fr.description: Emploi, accessibilité, culture : le président français, Emmanuel Macron, a annoncé vendredi une série de mesures pour améliorer la vie quotidienne des personnes handicapées et leur inclusion dans la société, lors de la 7e Conférence Nationale du Handicap (CNH), sans toutefois préciser de budget pour les financer.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : l'ambassadeur américain appelle Israël à assurer la sécurité des Palestiniens
france24fr.description: Au cours d'une visite en Cisjordanie occupée, qu'il appelle Judée-Samarie, l'ambassadeur des États-Unis en Israël a rappelé aux autorités israéliennes que la sécurité des Palestiniens relevait de leur responsabilité. Mike Huckabee, un ancien pasteur évangélique chrétien, rendait visite à des Américano-Palestiniens.

france24fr.title: Corinne Lepage, une vie consacrée à la défense de l’environnement
france24fr.description: C’est la rentrée de l’émission “Avec Judith”. Pour ce premier épisode, Judith reçoit Corinne Lepage, ancienne ministre de l’Environnement, avocate et pionnière du droit environnemental. Elle revient sur cinquante ans de combats pour l’environnement et sur l’état de l’écologie aujourd’hui. Au fil de l’entretien, Corinne Lepage revient également sur les grands procès qui ont contribué à construire le droit de l’environnement, de l’Erika à la justice climatique, mais aussi sur le nucléaire, les éne

france24fr.title: La plateforme américaine de VTC, Uber, quitte le Nigeria après 12 ans d'activité
france24fr.description: Uber a annoncé son retrait immédiat du Nigeria et de l’Ouganda. En pleine restructuration mondiale, cette décision intervient surtout alors que la plateforme de VTC américaine a fortement perdu du terrain face à ses concurrents dans ces deux pays.

france24fr.title: Guerre au Soudan : les responsabilités étrangères pointées du doigt par un rapport de l'ONU
france24fr.description: “Il faut un embargo sur les armes étendu à tout le Soudan, et il doit être respecté.” Voilà en somme les conclusions du rapport des experts de l'ONU dévoilé au Conseil des Droits de l'Homme. Un rapport qui pointe aussi du doigt les responsabilités d'entités étrangères dans ce conflit qui dure depuis maintenant plus de trois ans. Analyse avec notre correspondant régional, Bastien Renouil.

france24fr.title: Manifestations Gen Z à Madagascar : l'ex-président du Sénat condamné à dix ans de prison
france24fr.description: À Madagascar, la justice frappe l'un des visages les plus redoutés de l'ancien régime. L'ex-président du Sénat, le général Richard Ravalomanana, a été condamné à dix ans de travaux forcés pour son rôle dans la répression sanglante des manifestations de la Gen Z, en septembre et octobre 2025.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : le centre de réfugiés de Durban attaqué
france24fr.description: En Afrique du Sud, les affrontements entre étrangers et sud-africains continuent. Les militants du mouvement March and March continuent de manifester toutes les semaines pour demander le départ des immigrés illégaux. Des militants de ce mouvement ont attaqué un groupe d'étrangers qui s'étaient installés depuis trois mois devant le centre de réfugiés de Durban.

france24fr.title: Reportage au Népal : à la rencontre des survivants de la crue meurtrière
france24fr.description: De nos envoyés spéciaux à Katmandou – Au Népal, des milliers de personnes ont tout perdu en quelques minutes lors de la crue soudaine du 26 août. Depuis, les autorités, les ONG et les volontaires se mobilisent pour acheminer de l’aide aux sinistrés. Les envoyés spéciaux de France 24 se sont rendus dans un camp d’hébergement temporaire installé dans une école du district de Rasuwa, proche de l’épicentre de la catastrophe.

france24fr.title: Epidémie de rougeole au Bangladesh : plus de 1 000 enfants sont morts
france24fr.description: Au Bangladesh, l'épidémie de rougeole, une des plus meurtrières jamais recensées dans le pays, a bientôt fait un millier de morts en six mois et les hôpitaux du pays ne désemplissent pas. Depuis le mois de mars, plus de 180 000 personnes ont contracté cette maladie.

france24fr.title: Congrès du parti d'extrême droite Reform UK : marché conclu entre Farage et Bardella
france24fr.description: La conférence de rentrée de la formation d’extrême droite Reform UK a été marquée par la révélation de tentatives de contournement de la loi de financement des partis. Jordan Bardella, président du RN et invité d’honneur, a signé avec Nigel Farage un "protocole d’accord" pour lutter contre l’immigration illégale.

france24fr.title: "Wallace et Gromit” : le studio Aardman Animation fête ses 50 ans
france24fr.description: Le légendaire studio Aardman Animation, à l'origine de succès tels que “Wallace et Gromit”, fête cette année son 50e anniversaire. Avec la sortie prochaine d'un nouveau film “Shaun le mouton”, le studio continue de s'imposer en utilisant les mêmes techniques d'animation image par image que celles qu'il emploie depuis sa création.

spiegel.description: Nach zwölf Jahren ohne Unfall kam es nun bei der »Athens Flying Week« zur Tragödie: Ein griechischer Kampfjet stürzte ab. Beide Piloten kamen ums Leben.

spiegel.title: Russlanddeutsche vor der Wahl: »In Sachsen-Anhalt habe ich Toleranz gelernt«
spiegel.description: Erst wurde ihre Familie in Russland verfolgt, weil sie deutsch war. Heute wird Olga Ebert in Deutschland als Ausländerin beschimpft und erlebt, wie alte Wunden wieder aufbrechen.

spiegel.title: Oasis in Venedig: Liam und Noel Gallagher schwänzen Pressekonferenz
spiegel.description: Beim Filmfest Venedig präsentieren die krawalligen Gallagher-Brüder eine Doku über ihre Versöhnung. Doch die Oasis-Pressekonferenz musste ohne Oasis auskommen.

spiegel.title: Wasserstoff: Der Bodenschatz für den nächsten Goldrausch?
spiegel.description: Wasserstoff gilt als vielversprechender, sauberer Energieträger, womöglich lässt er sich viel einfacher gewinnen als bisher angenommen. Verblüffend ist vor allem, wie man ihn in freier Natur aufspüren kann.

spiegel.title: Michael Mendl ist tot: Mal charming man, mal bad boy
spiegel.description: Er kam zwar erst spät zum Film, setzte sich mit seiner charaktervollen Art aber schon bald in vielen Zuschauerköpfen fest: Die vielseitige Karriere von Michael Mendl in Bildern.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: USA und China planen angeblich Gespräche über KI-Sicherheit
spiegel.description: Wie gefährlich ist moderne KI? Das wird in den USA, aber auch China viel diskutiert. Schon bald, berichtet die Nachrichtenagentur Reuters, könnten die beiden Großmächte gemeinsam darüber sprechen.

spiegel.title: Frauke Brosius-Gersdorf: Warum ihre gescheiterte Wahl Demokratie stärkt
spiegel.description: Die Juraprofessorin erklärt ihre gescheiterte Kandidatur für das Verfassungsgericht zu einer tiefen Systemkrise. In Wahrheit ist der Vorgang der Beleg für eine funktionierende Demokratie.

spiegel.title: Post-Holiday-Blues: Drei Wege, wie das Urlaubsgefühl länger anhält
spiegel.description: Kaum zurück aus dem Urlaub, ist die Erholung oft schon wieder verflogen. Drei Wege, wie das entspannte Gefühl länger hält und das Post-Holiday-Syndrom gar nicht erst entsteht.

spiegel.title: Xiaomi SU7 auf der IFA in Berlin: China Speed am Funkturm
spiegel.description: In China sind die E-Autos von Xiaomi Kult. Nun bestaunt erstmals das Publikum in Deutschland die »Smartphones auf Rädern«. Die Technikmesse Ifa zeigt: Auf VW und Co. kommen schwere Zeiten zu.

spiegel.title: Belugawale in Kanada: Rettung nach Schließung von Freizeitpark »Marineland«
spiegel.description: Der bankrotte kanadische Freizeitpark Marineland drohte mit der Einschläferung von 30 Belugawalen, sollte staatliche Unterstützung ausbleiben. Stattdessen kam es nun zu einer spektakulären Rettungsaktion.

spiegel.title: Gamescom: Kölner Spielemesse gesteht Fehler im Umgang mit Technikklau ein
spiegel.description: Mehreren Indie-Entwicklern wurde auf der weltgrößten Spielemesse Hardware gestohlen, ein Betroffener trauerte vor der Kamera. Das Gamescom-Team konstatiert jetzt, es habe auf die Vorfälle zu herzlos reagiert.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Hacker veröffentlichen 1,4 Millionen sensible Daten im Darknet
spiegel.description: Eine Hackergruppe forderte rund zwei Millionen Euro Lösegeld von Berlin. Das Land zahlte nicht, nun stehen 1,4 Millionen teils äußerst sensible Daten im Darknet. Was passiert jetzt?

spiegel.title: 2. Bundesliga: VfL Wolfsburg verspielt 3:0-Führung gegen Energie Cottbus
spiegel.description: Bundesliga-Absteiger gegen Drittliga-Aufsteiger, acht Tore, aber freuen darf sich über dieses Spektakel nur Energie Cottbus: Der Außenseiter ließ sich von einem deutlichen Rückstand beim VfL nicht beirren.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: US-Unterhändler in Moskau gelandet – Treffen mit Putin geplant
spiegel.description: Erst Moskau, dann Kyjiw: Die USA nehmen ihre Friedensbemühungen im Ukrainekrieg wieder auf. Im Rahmen der Besuche sollen laut Putin die russischen Angriffe auf Kyjiw wohl drei Tage lang ruhen.

spiegel.title: Trans Mann in AfD-Hochburg Sachsen-Anhalt: Die geheime Verwandlung des Julian Kern
spiegel.description: Deshalb hat er sich für ein Geheimprojekt entschieden.

spiegel.title: Bananen: Wie Forschende in den Niederlanden sie retten wollen
spiegel.description: Forschende in den Niederlanden wollen die Banane retten, denn sie ist bedroht: Krankheitserreger könnten die Pflanzen auf Plantagen ausrotten. Um das zu verhindern, müssen sich Bananenarten paaren.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt - News zur Landtagswahl: Tausende Menschen demonstrieren in Magdeburg für eine weltoffene Gesellschaft
spiegel.description: Verwirrung um eine Deutschlangflagge: Siegmund poltert über ein entferntes Graffiti vor dem Magdeburger Dom, das gar nicht entfernt wurde. Was ist da los? Und: Auch in Magdeburg demonstrieren Tausende für eine weltoffene Gesellschaft. Das News-Update.

spiegel.title: Erni Mangold ist tot: Schauspielerin aus Österreich wurde 99 Jahre alt
spiegel.description: Sie arbeitete mit Gustaf Gründgens, aber auch mit Richard Linklater: Nun ist die österreichische Charakterdarstellerin Erni Mangold gestorben – im Alter von 99 Jahren.

observador.title: Águia volta ao Funchal à procura da quinta vitória seguida
observador.description: O Benfica quer responder à vitória do FC Porto na Madeira, frente ao recém promovido Marítimo, que somou sete pontos em quatro jornadas. Marco Silva lança João Palhinha no onze. Siga aqui em direto.

observador.title: La Pandera trouxe uma surpresa e o melhor João
observador.description: A 14.ª etapa chegou com novo triunfo na fuga e a melhor prestação de João, com direito a Almeidada em La Pandera. Brenner venceu pela primeira vez numa Grande Volta e Mas defendeu vermelha.

observador.title: Presidente moçambicano lança programa para gerar emprego
observador.description: O chefe de Estado moçambicano afirmou que a criação de postos de trabalho para jovens e mulheres constitui uma das prioridades centrais da atual governação.

observador.title: Governo sérvio homenageia criminoso de guerra Ratko Mladic
observador.description: Os restos mortais de Ratko Mladic foram transportados para a Sérvia num avião do governo e recebidos em Belgrado na quinta-feira com honras militares. Cerimónia criou mal estar entre Belgrado e a UE.

observador.title: Presidente sérvio vai concorrer a primeiro-ministro
observador.description: Vucic já tinha anunciado no dia 20 que anteciparia as eleições previstas para o final de 2027 em quase um ano, e especulou sobre a possibilidade de se candidatar, mas agora confirmou a sua candidatura

observador.title: Transportes. Portuenses valorizam mais as conexões que preço
observador.description: O preço surge como segunda razão, seguido da rapidez e da frequência. Ida do plano a consulta pública vai ser votada na reunião pública da Câmara do Porto de terça-feira.

observador.title: Europa não conseguirá suportar guerra prolongada com Rússia
observador.description: Numa cimeira organizada pela Conferência de Segurança de Munique, oficiais da NATO assumiram pessimismo com a preparação do continente europeu para uma possível guerra aberta com a Rússia.

observador.title: 16h. EUA atacam petroleiros iranianos após ataque do Irão
observador.description: Comando Central dos Estados Unidos diz que o ataque é uma mensagem para o regime de Teerão. Ainda, vários nomes cancelam presença no festival Commedia a La Carte Fest, que se realiza em outubro.

observador.title: Espanha controla porto de Ceuta para alojar migrantes
observador.description: Decreto permite a instalação de tendas numa superfície de 16 mil metros quadrados de área pública portuária, para alojar temporariamente mais de mil migrantes.

observador.title: Estacionamento: Porto perde anualmente 100 milhões
observador.description: Em causa estão números baseados nos reboques feitos pela Polícia Municipal, que recolhe "anualmente cerca de 15.000 veículos, uma média de cinco veículos por reboque por dia".

observador.title: A recusa de Cristina Peri Rossi
observador.description: Com "A Insubmissa", lançado originalmente em 2020, a Antígona vem dar início à publicação em Portugal da obra de uma das autoras latino-americanas mais conceituadas.

observador.title: Governo diz que Portugal cumpriu as metas do PRR na Cultura
observador.description: Segundo o Governo, foram concluídas intervenções em 83 museus, monumentos e palácios públicos, mais dois do que os 81 previstos. Até ao final do ano serão 90 os equipamentos intervencionados.

observador.title: Manifestações pela democracia na Alemanha antes das eleições
observador.description: Alguns milhares de pessoas manifestaram-se em Magdeburgo pela "democracia", na véspera da eleição na Saxónia-Anhalt (leste), onde a extrema-direita poderá ter uma vitória histórica.

observador.title: 15h. Médio do FC Porto já teve alta do Hospital de S. João
observador.description: Internacional dinamarquês sofreu uma concussão cerebral no jogo do FC Porto com o Moreirense. Ainda, Presidente russo determina suspensão dos ataques a Kiev durante três dias.

observador.title: Raras, mas muito letais. O que são as amebas?
observador.description: Quando inaladas, as amebas podem causar formas graves de meningite. Os casos são raros mas, na grande maioria dos casos, fatais. Em Portugal, há registo de um caso na região Norte em 2006.

observador.title: Festival F: como se constrói o evento numa zona histórica
observador.description: Os moradores deixam de ter estacionamento, há locais onde nada pode ser afixado e edifícios abertos ao público durante três dias. A 11.ª edição do evento termina este sábado na Vila Adentro.

observador.title: Ataques na Cisjordânia: Netanyahu está a fazer “teatro”?
observador.description: Com sondagens desfavoráveis, Netanyahu e o partido Likud precisam de apelar ao voto conservador e expandir ocupação da Cisjordânia até à ida às urnas. Oposição critica "cumplicidade" com a violência.

observador.title: 14h. Putin anuncia suspensão de ataques a Kiev
observador.description: A suspensão dos ataques vai acontecer durante 3 dias. Tadej Pogacar renovou contrato com a Emirates até 2032.

elpais.description: El realojo del puerto estaba pactado con la ciudad, que se ha echado atrás en el último momento y lo ha rechazado en el consejo de administración de la infraestructura. Puente firma una orden autorizando la medida

elpais.title: Bienvenidos al “patriarcado mediterráneo”: el exgeneral Vannacci pone en jaque a la derecha italiana
elpais.description: El nuevo partido de ultraderecha, Futuro Nacional, ya supera en los sondeos a la Liga y Forza Italia, los dos socios de coalición de Meloni, y el Gobierno maquina un nuevo sistema electoral para neutralizarlo

elpais.title: En este pueblo ganó AfD su primer alcalde de Alemania y desde entonces no para de crecer
elpais.description: Vecinos de Raguhn-Jessnitz dan por hecho que la extrema derecha obtendrá en el municipio más del 60% de los votos en las elecciones de Sajonia-Anhalt

elpais.title: Un contenedor marítimo convertido en hogar: historia de la casa más especial del Mar Menor
elpais.description: El arquitecto Javier Peña convirtió una casa estrecha en un terreno pequeño en un hogar espacioso gracias a una idea llamativa: usar un contenedor marítimo como último piso y dormitorio

elpais.title: Dustin Hoffman: “El éxito es más fácil que la felicidad”
elpais.description: A sus 89 años recién cumplidos, el actor que cambió la concepción de lo que es un galán ha escrito sus memorias y se enfrenta a un mundo en el que grandes amigos y compañeros ya no están

elpais.title: Tadej Pogacar no volverá a correr más en lo que queda de año tras la caída que sufrió en La Vuelta
elpais.description: UAE, equipo del esloveno, anuncia que el corredor se centrará en la recuperación de su clavícula izuquierda y de la vértebra cervical dañada. La estructura comunica además la renovación de su estrella hasta 2032

elpais.title: Por qué no se repitió el penalti que falló Mbappé: el detalle de la norma y la pillería de Bartra
elpais.description: Los árbitros aclaran que para que se considere que un defensa se ha adelantado al lanzamiento debe estar pisando el área, y el central lo había consultado días antes a un colegiado amigo

elpais.title: Hallada en Albacete la cabeza de una escultura de un joven íbero del siglo IV a. C.
elpais.description: La pieza encontrada en el yacimiento de Libisosa fue reutilizada por los romanos cuatro siglos después para levantar un muro del foro

elpais.title: El verano con más ahogamientos desde que hay registros: ¿cómo reconocer a alguien en peligro?
elpais.description: Entre junio y agosto han fallecido 239 personas en playas, piscinas, pantanos o ríos. Explicamos las claves para distinguir si una persona se está ahogando y cómo actuar

elpais.title: Estados Unidos bombardea tres petroleros iraníes, uno de ellos cerca de la estratégica isla de Jarg, en respuesta a ataques de Teherán
elpais.description: Según Washington, la República Islámica lanzó previamente misiles contra dos buques de guerra que patrullaban en la zona

elpais.title: Putin y Zelenski ordenan detener los ataques hasta el lunes por la visita de los enviados de Trump
elpais.description: El empresario Steve Witkoff y el yerno de Trump, Jared Kushner, llegaron a Moscú y viajarán el domingo a Kiev con el objetivo de reactivar las negociaciones de paz

elpais.title: Rusia usa arrestos y coacciones para lograr mandar más reclutas al frente con Ucrania
elpais.description: Las ONG denuncian un aumento de los abusos por parte de los reclutadores cuyos objetivos son a menudo personas vulnerables. Según los analistas Moscú registra unas 20.000 bajas al mes

nyt.title: Inside the D.O.J.’s Investigation of Fauci and Other Virus Scientists
nyt.description: As Dr. Anthony Fauci has faced public scrutiny from congressional Republicans, the D.O.J. has pursued a quieter and more expansive effort against a wider circle of researchers.

nyt.title: In Major Leak Hunt, Pentagon Gives Polygraph Tests to Joint Staff Members
nyt.description: About 50 people were tested, an unparalleled inquiry that comes in the wake of news reports about the war with Iran and the U.S. military’s diminished stocks of munitions.

nyt.title: U.S. Strikes Three Iranian ‘Shadow Network’ Oil Tankers, Military Says
nyt.description: The U.S. military said it retaliated after Iran launched missiles at two warships. The strikes came days after the two sides exchanged some of their most intense fire in weeks.

nyt.title: What the War in Iran Has Cost One Gold Star Family
nyt.description: First Lt. Tyler James Feehan, who was 25, had been deployed to an air base in Jordan when enemy missiles and drones lit up the sky. He is among the 18 Americans who have died since the war began.

nyt.title: Putin Orders Pause in Kyiv Strikes Ahead of Visit by U.S. Envoys
nyt.description: Steve Witkoff, President Trump’s special envoy, and Jared Kushner, his son-in-law, arrived in Moscow to meet with the Russian leader. They head to Kyiv next, in an effort to revive peace talks.

nyt.title: Putin Denies a Draft Is Coming, but Some Russian Men Are Taking No Chances
nyt.description: As the fear of a possible mobilization becomes a fixture of daily life across Russia, many men are deciding whether to flee, hide or sit tight.

nyt.title: What Will Happen to Lindsay Clancy in the Long Term?
nyt.description: Even as a jury failed to reach a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial, her future is unlikely to include freedom, at least for a long time. But Americans have been divided over the goal of her confinement.

nyt.title: In Complex Cases Like Lindsay Clancy’s, a Unanimous Verdict Can Be Hard to Reach
nyt.description: Hung juries are not common, but the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy was emotionally wrenching and uniquely complicated.

nyt.title: What Led to Maria Bartiromo’s Downfall at Fox News
nyt.description: The network this week took Maria Bartiromo off the air, pulling one of the last hosts whose coverage of Dominion Voting Systems drew an expensive defamation lawsuit.

nyt.title: In Red States, Law-and-Order Republicans Turn Against Flock Cameras
nyt.description: The governors of Texas and Florida have taken steps to curtail the use of license-plate readers, even as the police say they help with solving crime.

nyt.title: Gallup Polls Show Democrats Outnumber Republicans Ahead of 2026 Midterm Elections
nyt.description: Data from Gallup shows that Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents have their largest advantage over Republicans since 2008.

nyt.title: Missouri Asks Supreme Court to Allow Voting Map Benefiting Republicans
nyt.description: Missouri’s Supreme Court said a map redrawn to help Republicans could not be used in November and said voters should decide on the new boundaries.

nyt.title: Ossoff and Talarico to Share Fund-Raising Event in Hollywood

nyt.description: At the U.S. Open she is playing a whole new style game.

nyt.description: Even a very successful thriller writer fights self-doubt. His new tough-talking writing guide doubles as a memoir that explains why, and how to beat it.

nyt.title: Notre Dame’s Jersey Patch Deal With SoFi Divides Alumni and Fans
nyt.description: Alumni have varying opinions about the school’s deal with the personal finance company SoFi to advertise on Notre Dame athletic uniforms.

nyt.title: The Purest American Culture Lives on at Local Festivals
nyt.description: Turning hyperlocal traditions into public spectacle is a U.S. pastime.

nyt.title: Scenic Route
nyt.description: The season’s new releases give us a cultural road map, but the most rewarding reading, listening and watching comes from the detours.

npr.title: US military hits 3 Iranian oil tankers after saying Navy warships were targeted
npr.description: The strikes come a day after President Trump appeared to downplay the war with Iran as "small potatoes" during an exchange with reporters in the Oval Office.

npr.title: How the U.S. focus on Iran is fueling a more aggressive Putin
npr.description: Trump's top envoys head to Moscow and Kyiv as Putin steps up round the clock bombing of Ukraine. With the U.S. distracted by Iran, is Putin becoming increasingly emboldened?

npr.title: U.S. envoys in Moscow in new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
npr.description: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have arrived in Moscow to revive efforts to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called for a halt to air attacks during their visit, but Moscow has not publicly responded.

npr.title: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posts bail after arrest
npr.description: Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte has posted bail after order issued for her arrest on charges she publicly threatened to arrange assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two others.

npr.title: The U.N. backs a new world map showing Africa in its true relative size
npr.description: The U.N. has backed a new map showing Africa in its true relative size, with the U.S. standing alone in opposition.

npr.title: Philippine vice president is ordered arrested for threats against the president
npr.description: It's part of a political showdown with Marcos. A trial could impact her plans to run for president in 2028.

npr.title: Myanmar military head visits Vietnam to normalize relations
npr.description: His trip to Vietnam marks his third visit to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore Myanmar's standing in the bloc.

npr.title: Trump asks SCOTUS to OK changes to mail-in ballots. And, diesel prices hit record high
npr.description: Trump has asked the Supreme Court to lift the block on his plan for the USPS to restrict mail voting ahead of the midterm elections. And, diesel prices have reached a record high.

npr.title: Germany's far-right AfD party is poised for power in a state election
npr.description: Germany's AfD's TikTok-fueled rise in Saxony-Anhalt is raising fears the country could see its first far-right governor since World War II.

npr.description: In Ukraine, a week of near-continuous Russian attacks is upending the lives of residents in Kyiv and its suburbs.

phys-org.title: Tree species diversity protects forests from climate extremes, study finds
phys-org.description: New research has found that tree species diversity can play a crucial role in protecting forests from the growing threat of extreme climate events. The study analyzed data from 88,116 separate forest plots across the United States to investigate the impact of "compound climate extremes," when events such as drought and extreme heat occur at the same time.

phys-org.title: Scientists discover how narwhals grow nature's only straight tusk
phys-org.description: Narwhals have nature's only straight tusk, a single tooth up to three meters (10 feet) long, so strange they were sold as magical unicorn horns during the Middle Ages.

phys-org.title: Some disagreement makes groups more trustworthy, mathematical framework finds
phys-org.description: When humans are making decisions, they are known not to rely solely on their own considerations and the evidence available to them. Past behavioral science and psychology studies have shown that people are often also influenced by the choices and opinions of others.

phys-org.title: Lakes aren't just storing water—they're changing the carbon cycle
phys-org.description: Lakes may look like picturesque stopping points along a river or stream, but they can have a big influence on what happens to carbon as it moves through a landscape. New research suggests that the more lake-rich a network of streams is, the more carbon is released into the atmosphere rather than carried downstream.

phys-org.title: Ocean indicators NOAA scientists are tracking for El Niño's arrival on the West Coast
phys-org.description: Has El Niño reached the West Coast? You might think it has. After all, the ocean off Southern and Central California is unusually warm. But that warmth is from a recent marine heat wave that predates the current El Niño. Much of the Pacific Coast is experiencing relatively normal conditions while still awaiting the impacts of what could be a very strong El Niño.

phys-org.title: Late Roman decrees uncover military system behind amphitheater animal spectacles
phys-org.description: A study on Roman law by the Carlos III University of Madrid analyzes the regulations and complex imperial logistics governing the capture, transport and safety of animals used in spectacles in the Roman Empire—which were far more popular than gladiatorial combat.

phys-org.title: New method predicts where massive earthquakes will strike
phys-org.description: UC Riverside scientists have developed a way to identify where Earth's biggest earthquakes are most likely to occur, offering a powerful new tool for improving disaster preparation in some of the most dangerous seismic regions.

phys-org.title: How haze from Indonesian fires impacts Southeast Asia
phys-org.description: Thick smog has blanketed parts of Indonesia as the vast archipelago battles fires that have burned large swaths of Borneo and Sumatra for weeks.

phys-org.title: Indonesia rescues second orangutan mother and baby from wildfire
phys-org.description: An orangutan mother and her baby, threatened by wildfires encroaching on their habitat in Indonesia, were rescued earlier this week, authorities said in a statement Saturday.

phys-org.title: Spacecraft bound for Mercury begins 'tricky' arrival
phys-org.description: After an eight-year journey, a spacecraft carrying European and Japanese probes began the monthslong, high-risk approach to Mercury on Thursday to study the sun-scorched planet.

phys-org.title: Levitated magnet opens new frontier in search for ultraheavy dark matter
phys-org.description: Rice University researchers have used a magnetically levitated particle to search for ultraheavy dark matter, extending the hunt for some of the heaviest possible forms of the invisible matter thought to hold galaxies together. Led by Christopher Tunnell, associate professor of physics and astronomy, the researchers used a tiny floating magnet as a highly sensitive detector designed to register the faint push an ultraheavy dark matter particle could produce as it passed through.

phys-org.title: AI could undermine managers' judgment unless used carefully, study warns
phys-org.description: Generative artificial intelligence (Gen-AI) has become a routine part of working life, but overreliance on the technology may erode managers' ability to build moral insights, contextual understanding and know-how to get a job done, according to a new study from the University of Bath.

phys-org.title: Study reveals pupils most at risk of school suspension and what may help them
phys-org.description: School suspensions are associated with a complex combination of socioeconomic disadvantage, special educational needs, peer relationships and students' experiences of school, according to new research from The University of Manchester.

phys-org.title: Deadly floods of 2021—Researchers identify gaps in hazard mapping
phys-org.description: The catastrophic flooding in July 2021 claimed the lives of more than 200 people in Germany and Belgium. The high death toll makes it clear that hazard mapping and risk communication must be improved urgently. Researchers at the University of Potsdam, the Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, the University of Louvain and Johns Hopkins University analyzed the locations and specific circumstances of 224 deaths. Their findings show that many occurred outside the officially mapped flood hazard zones an

Researchers from MIT Lincoln Laboratory heard some of this cacophony when analyzing data from commercial off-the-shelf sensors that they integrated and deployed in 2024 during the U.S. Navy's Operation Ice Camp (OIC). This past March, during OIC 2026, the researchers returned to the Arctic with a higher-fidelity version of one

phys-org.title: A new type of LED light could bring significant efficiency gains
phys-org.description: Researchers at Lund University have developed a new type of light-emitting diode based on thin, branched nanowires that could offer significantly higher efficiency and lower production costs than current technology. By controlling where in the structure the light is generated, the researchers have reduced the losses that would otherwise limit the amount of light that can be used. Their study is published in the journal Nano Research.

phys-org.title: In ant nervous systems, gene expression may drive rescue behavior
phys-org.description: Why do some ants help nestmates in distress while others don't? A research team from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) and Tel Aviv University addressed this question in a new study. The researchers examined worker ants of the species Cataglyphis niger, some of which had shown rescue behavior while others had not. The results, recently published in the Journal of Experimental Biology, suggest that the key difference lies not in body size, morphology or the animals' energy reser

phys-org.title: Magic-angle graphene provides evidence for unconventional superconductivity
phys-org.description: Researchers have completely suppressed superconductivity in magic-angle graphene by screening interactions between electrons, helping resolve a long-running debate about the origin of the phenomenon.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.

proj-syn.title: Asia’s Natural Disasters Must Not Become Financial Crises
proj-syn.description: The dangerous flooding in Nepal and Tibet has demonstrated, once again, the need for prearranged disaster-risk financing to prepare for the economic chain reactions triggered by natural disasters. Asia’s policymakers must act now to help cash-strapped Nepal and strengthen other countries’ resilience before the next crisis hits.

proj-syn.title: Is AI Crowding Out Other Investment?
proj-syn.description: The AI investment boom has unleashed a wave of demand for capital just as savings are declining and interest rates remain high. As competition for financing intensifies, rising borrowing costs could squeeze non-AI firms looking to finance new factories, equipment, and projects.

proj-syn.title: India’s Resilience Depends on Diversified Trade
proj-syn.description: India has signed a flurry of trade deals since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in an attempt to ensure that no single bilateral rupture will cause catastrophic harm. It should continue to expand its trade ties, while being wary of any bilateral agreement that curtails its freedom of action vis-à-vis third countries.

proj-syn.title: Whipsaw Trade Policy Is Depressing Foreign Direct Investment
proj-syn.description: If a country opts for higher trade restrictions to promote its perceived domestic interests, a predictable policy is far superior to a volatile one. As new research shows, uncertainty causes unnecessary and large collateral damage to FDI inflows.

proj-syn.title: Why the Far Right’s War on Modern Architecture Matters
proj-syn.description: The Alternative for Germany’s fixation on architecture is more revealing than it may seem. Cultural policy is not only one area where the party can actually change conditions on the ground at the state level; it is also intimately tied to far-right forces’ exclusionary political agenda.

proj-syn.title: How Will the US-Iran War End?
proj-syn.description: The latest US effort to subdue Iran—an "economic D-Day" intended to cut off the Islamic Republic from the world economy—can’t succeed without the support of the country’s biggest trade partner. The only stable solution to the impasse in the Gulf is one that involves China and increases economic integration in the region.

proj-syn.title: Germany’s Political Firewall Is Crumbling
proj-syn.description: The upcoming election in Saxony-Anhalt could give the far-right Alternative für Deutschland control of a state government for the first time in Germany’s postwar history. Its rise offers a crucial lesson for democracies elsewhere: closing ranks against extremist parties is no substitute for effective governance.

proj-syn.title: The Swimmable City Test
proj-syn.description: In committing to provide a safe swimmable place within 15 minutes of every home by 2035, London Mayor Sadiq Khan has set a measurable, time-bound goal that cannot be met through a single program or line item on the budget. Instead, it requires a public mission capable of mobilizing all ministries and shaping markets.

proj-syn.title: The Tale of Economics
proj-syn.description: A new book tells the story of the economics discipline and its original purpose with a degree of verve and imaginativeness that puts dreary mainstream economists to shame. In the process, it gets at fundamental truths that major schools within the discipline have managed to obscure.

proj-syn.title: AI’s Market Path Will Get Bumpier
proj-syn.description: By enhancing the input that goes into so much of what we do—intelligence—AI’s potential to drive higher economic growth is enormous. But with fears of the technology's unintended consequences affecting the pace and depth of adoption, the promise of long-term gains must be set against more immediate risks.

proj-syn.title: American Götterdämmerung
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump and his Treasury secretary’s latest desperate threats confirm how much American power has waned on their watch. Far from compelling others to join their efforts to isolate Iran, they are hastening the transition to a post-American world order.

proj-syn.title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
proj-syn.description: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
proj-syn.description: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

proj-syn.title: Building Canada’s Post-American Economy
proj-syn.description: Canada’s dependence on the US market has become a strategic liability, leaving it vulnerable to President Donald Trump’s bullying. Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.
